title: Label-only output does not prevent membership inference by a label-aware attacker

invariants.description: Label-only output must still significantly reduce correct decisions of the recalibrated threshold attack (observed p ≈ 3e-15; significant on 20/20 seeds).
Consumers keep the same decisions (observed 0.725, identical to the undefended service); ranking utility is lost.

DOCUMENTED DEFENSE FAILURE: an attacker who knows the label still gains ≥ 0.2 advantage from 'was it classified correctly' (observed 0.280; 20-seed range 0.256–0.332): the training/test accuracy gap itself leaks membership.
Leakage must still be claimed against label-only output (observed p ≈ 1e-19; claimed on 20/20 seeds).

rationale: Hiding the score removes the confidence signal but not correctness: an overfit model is right on (almost) all members and wrong on ~28% of non-members. Output restriction is not differential privacy (deterministic release, ε = ∞); only reducing the generalisation gap addresses this signal.
